title: Return statements inside constructors
answer: A constructor may use a bare `return;` statement to end constructor execution early, but it cannot return a value because constructors have no return type. Any fields not explicitly assigned before the bare return keep the values established by default initialization or earlier initializers. Using early returns in constructors can make invariants harder to understand, so validation followed by clear initialization is usually preferable.
